findings.quote: Tuning can cost more than the bronze on a small bell, and less than it on a heavy one.
findings.note: Labour-vs-metal economics (metal cost scales with mass, lathe labour far less so) makes D the true real-world statement, and it is also the only two-sided conditional among three flat generalisations ('always takes a larger share', 'a single price for each kilo', 'far longer to tune'). The distractors are substantive trade claims a passage would have to decide, so this is world-knowledge answerability, not a form-only leak.

findings.quote: The bell has to leave the mould heavier, since the metal tuning removes must be there first.
findings.note: Standard founding practice - bells are cast with a tuning allowance because lathe tuning only removes metal - decides A on domain knowledge, and A's own justifying clause is close to self-evident. B, C and D are substantive claims a passage would still have to ground, so flag rather than a structural leak.

findings.quote: He treats the disagreement as a matter of taste that measurement can never settle.
findings.note: Two options fall passage-blind: B is undercut because A and C both presuppose an actual trial exists, and D's 'workshop folklore that the measurements have already disposed of' is the overreaching dismissal typical of filler. A (mild lean) versus C (even-handed) stays undecided without the text; lean C on expository-genre convention.

findings.quote: How a bell's partials are tuned, what that work costs, and how far founders take it.
findings.note: Main-idea item in which D is the compound scope statement that largely subsumes A's cost angle, while B ('recover less of the bronze ... than they generally suppose') is too narrow to be a thesis and C lists a different text's subject. Breadth-wins is a form-level tell, but A remains a live competitor if the text really is price-focused, so partial rather than decided.

findings.quote: It has been occupied every single summer since the boxes first went up on that gable.
findings.note: 'every single summer' is the scalar overreach of C's hedged twin ('most summers'); in an absolute/hedged pair of the same claim the hedged member is the test-wise pick, which lifts C well above chance from form alone. B and D (fitting date, logging span) remain live, so the item is not decided blind.

findings.quote: Cast boxes work as well as timber ones provided they are hung high on a sunny wall.
findings.note: C contradicts the stem's own presupposition that only two cast boxes were occupied, and D ('gave up its heat more quickly') would predict worse rather than better occupancy - both drop passage-blind. A's 'not by the boxes' is the canonical confound inference for a 'suggests' item, but A over B is a lean only.

findings.quote: Convinced: the writer agrees with her that what a box is made of hardly matters at all.
findings.note: The two absolute stances (A fully convinced, D fully dismissive) drop out against two qualified middles - a form-only elimination of half the set that needs no domain knowledge. B versus C is not decided without the text; lean B.

findings.quote: Why some purpose-built replacement roosts are taken up by bats while others stand empty.
findings.note: B is the only option framed as the article-thesis puzzle; C's 'give up counting animals altogether' is an absolute overreach and A and D name background specifics, so B sits well above chance from form alone in a main-idea item. A or D could still be the text's frame, so partial rather than decided.

findings.quote: Låntagaren fick säd och lämnade tillbaka lika mycket vid skörden, jämte ett tillägg på vanligen en åttondel.
findings.note: Knowledge of Swedish sockenmagasin (grain lent in spring, repaid in kind at harvest with a customary surcharge, commonly an eighth) picks C, and D's 'fördela risken mellan gårdarna' is a non sequitur since lending to everyone at once concentrates rather than spreads risk. The surcharge size varied by parish, so the passage still decides the detail - world knowledge, not pure recall.

findings.quote: Kyrkvärden förvarade båda nycklarna och kunde därför öppna magasinet utan att någon annan var närvarande.
findings.note: Magasinsordningar existed to impose dual control (two locks held by different men) and a running ledger, so B, C and D each describe the absence of a control an ordinance would prescribe, leaving A with its era-correct Mikaeli term. That reasoning is institutional/domain knowledge and a passage could report an unusual local arrangement, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Att han överdriver sparbankernas roll så till den grad att ingen enda av socknarna i boken stöder sambandet.
findings.note: C and D are the same criticism at two strengths and C carries the absolute ('ingen enda') - the classic near-duplicate pair in which the calibrated member is the key; D is additionally the only option whose subject is the förklaring the stem asks about ('Att den vilar...') while A, B and C are about the author. Above chance from form alone, but A and B stay possible.

findings.quote: För att ge läsaren en paus från bokens paragrafer och förteckningar; de är trevliga men utan betydelse för hennes omdöme om boken.
findings.note: A answers a purpose question with 'no purpose' and D overreaches ('varje byggnad ända fram till i dag'), so both drop blind. Residual hint: naming a spruthus and a lada in a review of a granary book implies the buildings outlived the institution, which is B's premise - far weaker than an outright presupposition, and B's evaluative point about Grimlund is not entailed, so B over C is a lean, not a decided leak.
